body:
Another bug, and this one has a lesson attached that I think matters more than the bug.

The API review identified R/crossnobis.R:230-232 as the single best error message in the package - the only one of 986 stop() calls that contains runnable code - and I filed a recommendation to rewrite roughly 40 other messages on its model. I then executed its advice. It fails twice.

The message:

  A learned crossnobis plan requires a residual-derived precision recipe;
  use noise_precision(diag(...)) for a fixed identity metric.

Following it literally:

  metric = noise_precision(diag(P))                  -> argument "domain" is missing, with no default
  metric = noise_precision(diag(P), domain = domain) -> Metric-recipe fields are missing or noncanonical

The suggested call omits a required argument, and once that is supplied the resulting object is rejected by the very function that suggested it. Cause: noise_precision() builds a FIXED neural metric, while plan_crossnobis() requires a metric RECIPE. The message routes the user out of the recipe family and into the fixed family while they are calling the function that only accepts recipes. shrinkage_precision() and diagonal_precision() both work.

THE LESSON, which is why I am sending this rather than just filing it. My remediation plan proposed copying this message shape 40 times. Had that been done before anyone executed it, the package would have acquired 40 authoritative-looking messages built on a template that does not run. Any process that rewrites these messages has to EXECUTE the suggested code, not merely review it for tone. A message containing code that fails is worse than one containing no code, because it carries more authority and costs the user more time before they distrust it.

I have noted that sequencing constraint on the error-message bead.

Third observation on the same seam, and this is now a pattern rather than three incidents. Today I have found: cross_partitions() silently mispairing a fit, plan_geometry refusing a fit while plan_crossnobis accepts one, and now the metric-recipe versus fixed-metric families being crossed by the package own advice. All three are the same boundary - relation versus fit, recipe versus fixed metric, geometry versus crossnobis - and it is the least documented region of the package. If any single area deserves attention before the 0.1 surface is frozen further, I think it is that seam, and it sits in your chain rather than in the usability workstream.

Filed as bd-01KZYJAQ7Y06F5C1P7KG6MAJE4 with reproduction.
